I found two details to tighten: bootstrap also returns the diff-workflow and push-integration services, and chat filtering removes specific fields rather than all history. I’ll use the peripheral trees to show resource lifetimes, MCP binding, streaming backpressure, and evaluation data dependencies.

Five peripheral trees expand resource ownership, MCP scope and write classification, chat visibility, live transport state, and evaluation data dependencies. Edges attach to the relevant concepts rather than arbitrary tree roots. Positions account for actual text dimensions and leave gaps.

The decomposition combines modular structure with call paths, ownership and data dependencies. Evidence comes only from the supplied point, seed and pinned source text. The lifetime tree follows bootstrap.ts and vitePlugin.ts; scope follows apiAccess.ts, agentRoutes.ts and infrastructure/mapping/mcp/server.ts; chat follows agentChatRoutes.ts; live follows liveCanvasRoutes.ts; evaluation follows bootstrap.ts and evalRoutes.ts.

Source-grounded corrections: bootstrap also exposes diffSessionWorkflows and pushIntegrations. Chat projection removes generation.history specifically, not all retained conversation history. Socket binding occurs on attach/publish messages; the implementation does not require the literal first received frame to establish a role. Final diagram-tool validation applies whenever there is no chat binding, including explicitly targeted connections. The comparison generation tool is named generate-diagram-comparisons. The peripherals also show details absent from the seed: fake comparison runtime selection, context source resolution, MCP readOnlyHint versus the narrower HTTP POST allowlist, context-request serialization, weak ETag matching, and evaluation response projections.
